assumptions: The opportunity is evaluated as a Poland-localized workflow add-on that links to authoritative inspection records; it does not perform, certify, or replace competent-person or UDT inspections.
The proposed 199/399/799 PLN monthly fleet tiers, optional claim-pack fee, 45000 PLN initial capital envelope, and three-to-five-hour daily founder commitment are the operative v2 model.

No Polish fleet demand, channel commitment, integration right, evidentiary acceptance, CAC, churn, support cost, or addressable fleet count is assumed beyond the supplied evidence; these remain uncertainties rather than evidence of failure.

A technically competent, AI-assisted founder can build and operate a bounded mobile-web MVP, while legal interpretation, bespoke integrations, field onboarding, and claim disputes require standardized scope or outside expertise.

The founder-net-worth scenario assumes substantial founder ownership, debt-light growth, competitive SaaS contribution margins, and successful reinvestment, but it is treated as a sensitivity rather than a forecast.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Equipment inspection, custody transfer, and damage allocation are genuine recurring events, and joining their evidence can reduce administrative friction. The insight is weakened because UDT already owns authoritative supervised-equipment records and multiple products already implement inspection-to-claim evidence; the remaining Polish localization and portability gap is an inference, not an established structural opening.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Ramirent's terms directly establish that damage can create recoverable repair, labour, parts, and downtime costs, while inspection obligations make recordkeeping recurrent. However, damage-dispute frequency, recoverability, administrative cost, and Polish fleets' willingness to pay for a separate add-on are unknown; existing lower-priced and bundled alternatives constrain plausible willingness to pay.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Fleet-tier SaaS can support attractive gross margins and recurring revenue, and the revised pricing is anchored near HireCheck rather than the untenable original per-asset price. Yet CAC, churn, onboarding and support burden, channel share, image and AI costs, claim-review labour, and payback are all unproven. The 5 million PLN founder-equity path requires roughly 1000 accounts at 500 PLN monthly, 30% EBITDA, and a 4x multiple, making scale, retention, and channel efficiency decisive rather than demonstrated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Small and mid-sized Polish rental fleets on one compatible platform form a specific, testable beachhead. Its economic sufficiency is unresolved because neither the count of fleets lacking equivalent features nor damage volume by asset class is known, and the required 1000-account scale may exceed the genuinely underserved Polish segment.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: HireCheck is a direct feature-level substitute, while InTempo, Texada, ToolSense, and Trackunit demonstrate that system-of-record vendors can embed the workflow. Polish regulatory adapters and accepted local exports might win a narrow niche, but there is no exclusive channel, proprietary right, or proven customer outcome that would let this add-on dominate it.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful embedded record could plausibly extend across adjacent asset classes, repair workflows, insurance claims, analytics, and nearby CEE jurisdictions. Those adjacencies become easier only after winning a system-of-record integration and proving evidentiary and recovery value, so expansion is plausible but presently conditional rather than validated.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Accumulated serial-level histories and workflow integration could create switching friction and useful data. Those benefits require repeated adoption and integration depth, while better-positioned rental platforms can bundle equivalent capture, own the primary customer data, and reproduce localization; a neutral duplicate ledger is especially vulnerable to low usage and churn.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The proposed offer may provide Polish document links, portable exports, and competitive fleet pricing, but no evidence shows materially better recovery, speed, compliance, usability, or total cost. Embedded competitors are more convenient by avoiding duplicate entry, and HireCheck already offers timestamps, GPS, signatures, history, integrations, and claim packs at a comparable price.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Mobile capture and AI assistance make a lean product feasible, and digital inspection and damage workflows are evidently active. The legal obligations are longstanding rather than a new catalyst, UDT has already digitized authoritative records, and the March 2026 Texada launch indicates incumbent momentum that benefits the category while narrowing the entrant's window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A five-to-ten-fleet pilot on one platform is bounded, and a software integrator, dealer, or insurer could eventually make acquisition repeatable. No partner willingness, integration access, reseller economics, CAC, or scalable route is evidenced, direct founder-led selling conflicts with the founder's preferred social load, and incumbent software vendors may already supply the feature.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A mobile-web MVP is technically compatible with the founder's data and AI skills, stated capital, and part-time validation constraint. The durable business is harder: integrations, yard adoption, statutory-boundary accuracy, GDPR controls, evidence disputes, onboarding, and support can exceed five hours daily or require partners and specialists. These are manageable validation risks, but several are central dependencies rather than peripheral tasks.

interaction_adjustment.rationale: The product needs deep incumbent integration both to distribute cheaply and to avoid duplicate-entry churn, yet the same system-of-record providers can bundle the feature or withhold access. That dependency compounds distribution, retention, and defensibility risk beyond the separate factor scores.

main_structural_strength: A recurring, legally and commercially anchored custody-and-damage workflow creates a concrete paid-event opportunity that can be tested with a capital-light product aligned to the founder's technical strengths.
primary_score_limiter: The proposal has no demonstrated right to win against an exact low-priced standalone substitute and several embedded incumbents, while its only plausible distribution and retention mechanism depends on uncommitted system-of-record channels.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: HireCheck already sells the core standalone proposition—timestamped and GPS-tagged photos, signatures, inspection history, rental-software integration, and one-click claim packs—with its 100-item year-two price around 417 PLN monthly; InTempo and other platforms additionally embed similar functions directly in the rental workflow.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A signed integration or reseller commitment from a Polish rental-software, dealer, or insurer channel, plus repeated paid pilots showing that currently underserved fleets complete the workflow, recover materially more damage or save measurable labour, retain at the revised pricing, and produce viable CAC, support cost, channel share, and payback economics.
highest_value_structural_change: Make the product an exclusive embedded Polish claims-and-regulatory adapter for one underserved rental platform or insurer, with contractually accepted exports and revenue tied partly to verified recovery, so distribution, workflow adoption, and differentiated evidentiary value come from the channel rather than from a parallel standalone ledger.
